content_units: Movie Night Shortlist for Four

Aiming for clever, upbeat, low-stress picks under   2h 15m  , with a blend of   comedy, mystery, and adventure   and no heavy gore, sexual content, jump scares, or bleak endings. These choices lean toward the same sweet spot as   Knives Out  ,   Paddington 2  ,   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse  , and   The Martian  .
Eight Strong Picks
Option 1:   See How They Run     A fast-talking 1950s whodunit about a murder in London’s theater world and the mismatched investigators trying to solve it.     98 min
-   Why it fits:   Closest to the  Knives Out  vibe here—light mystery, witty ensemble energy, and playful tone without getting grim.
-   Content caution:   One murder investigation with mild peril and some sarcastic meanness, but little onscreen violence.
Option 2:   Clue     Six suspicious dinner guests and a butler spiral into chaos when murder strikes a creepy mansion.     94 min
-   Why it fits:   A classic comic mystery with nonstop banter, zero jump-scare emphasis, and an intentionally silly tone.
-   Content caution:   Murder is central to the plot, but violence is bloodless and played for laughs.
Option 3:   The Princess Bride     A farm boy crosses swords, cliffs, and kidnappers to reunite with his true love.     98 min
-   Why it fits:   Adventure-comedy comfort food—funny, quotable, energetic, and warmly satisfying rather than emotionally draining.
-   Content caution:   Mild fantasy sword fights and peril; romance is sweet and very tame.
Option 4:   The Adventures of Tintin     A young reporter follows a model ship clue into a globe-trotting treasure hunt.     107 min
-   Why it fits:   Scratches the adventure puzzle itch with brisk momentum and family-friendly action.
-   Content caution:   Cartoon-style chases, gunfire, and danger, but not graphic or scary.
Option 5:   Enola Holmes     Sherlock Holmes’s teenage sister uses observation and nerve to solve a disappearance in Victorian England.     123 min
-   Why it fits:   Mystery-forward, charming, and energetic, with a smart lead and an easy crowd-pleasing tone.
-   Content caution:   Some fistfights and chase scenes; a few tense moments but no horror-style shocks.
Option 6:   Hunt for the Wilderpeople     A grumpy foster uncle and a rebellious kid become accidental fugitives in the New Zealand wilderness.     101 min
-   Why it fits:   Offbeat humor, heart, and adventure with a hopeful emotional landing rather than a sad one.
-   Content caution:   Brief references to loss and some comic-action danger, but overall gentle and upbeat.
Option 7:   Game Night     A friendly game evening turns into a real criminal mix-up that the players think is still part of the fun.     100 min
-   Why it fits:   Great for a group watch—very funny, mystery-adjacent, fast-moving, and packed with clever visual jokes.
-   Content caution:   Mild-to-moderate violence and crime comedy, with a few intense moments; still not gory or horror-like.
Option 8:   The Mitchells vs. the Machines     A chaotic family road trip becomes humanity’s accidental last hope during a robot uprising.     114 min
-   Why it fits:   If your group loved  Into the Spider-Verse , this has similarly inventive, high-energy animation and lots of heart.
-   Content caution:   Frequent animated action and sensory busyness, but no gore and no upsetting ending.
Best Match by Mood
-   Most like Knives Out:     See How They Run
-   Safest all-around crowd-pleaser:     The Princess Bride
-   Best animated pick:     The Mitchells vs. the Machines
-   Best comedy-first choice:     Game Night
-   Best adventure mystery blend:     Enola Holmes
